content.text:
Yes—**gardening can absolutely be art**, though it can also be craft, science, labor, design, ecology, or food production depending on intent and context.

If someone arranges plants, colors, textures, paths, seasons, light, scent, and space to create an experience or express an idea, gardening functions much like sculpture, architecture, or painting—but with living materials. A garden changes over time, so it can be a kind of **living, seasonal, participatory art**.

That said, not all gardening has to be art. Growing tomatoes efficiently, maintaining a lawn, or restoring habitat may be primarily practical or ecological. But even practical gardens can become artistic through choices of form, rhythm, contrast, composition, and meaning.

So the short answer is: **gardening is art when it is practiced with aesthetic, expressive, or experiential intention—and it remains one of the few arts that literally grows.**
